title: Meet M2 Lab: test the awkward enquiry
hooks: A perfect example tells you very little about a messy workday.
A polished demo can hide the one case your team actually worries about.
Your first test should include something awkward on purpose.
full_spoken_english: A perfect example tells you very little about a messy workday. Say you want AI to help turn enquiry notes into follow-up drafts. Make three fictional notes before you try it. One has every detail. One has no deadline. The third has two different deadlines. At M2 Lab, our Builds start with a small test like this. Decide what a useful result would look like before running it. Facts should stay unchanged. Missing details should stay visible. Conflicting dates should become a question for the person handling the enquiry. Compare the draft with the original note. A tidy paragraph still fails your test if it quietly chooses a date. Try the awkward cases before connecting the workflow. What is the missing detail that catches your team most often?
cta: Try the awkward cases before connecting the workflow. What is the missing detail that catches your team most often?

fixture.input: A: needs reply Tuesday. B: deadline missing. C: header says Tuesday; body says Thursday.
fixture.designed_output: A: Tuesday. B: deadline unknown. C: conflicting deadlines; ask enquiry owner.
fixture.check: Never silently resolve missing or contradictory dates.

audio_plan: Natural recorded voice; no imitation. Quiet room; optional subtle licensed music only after voice intelligibility check. No sound needed to understand proof panels.
caption_plan: Editable sentence captions, maximum two short lines; keep proof labels clear. Captions paraphrase nothing that changes a fact. Final platform safe-zone check after edit.
